result.title: Trajectory-Retrieval Speculative Decoding: When Does a Model's Own History Help?
result.summary: Long chain-of-thought reasoning increases sequential decoding cost while creating a growing history of potentially reusable continuations. We investigate when this history supplies useful drafts and complements an existing drafter. Controlled source comparisons reveal trajectory-specific reuse, motivating our method Trajectory-Local Adaptive Retrieval (TLAR). TLAR retrieves approximately matched continuations from the current trajectory and uses recent verification outcomes to adapt retrieval activation and candidate width. TLAR combines retrieved continuations with model-generated drafts in a shared candidate tree, preserving the target model's output distribution through exact verification. Across code debugging, mathematics, and open-ended writing, our evaluation connects source reuse, incremental acceptance, and execution cost. Combining TLAR with strong retrieval baselines improves token acceptance under matched verification budgets and increases end-to-end throughput over the draft-model baseline. These findings support generated trajectories as runtime memory for adaptive inference.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究长链式思维推理中模型自身历史轨迹能否提供可复用的草稿，提出 Trajectory-Local Adaptive Retrieval（TLAR），从当前轨迹检索近似匹配的续写并与模型草稿合并到候选树中，用验证结果自适应调节检索激活与候选宽度。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属纯文本推理加速的推测解码，但其「运行轨迹作为运行时记忆、检索复用、用验证反馈调节计算量」的思路，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态复用、动态计算与轨迹记忆的可借鉴线索，需人工核查其检索粒度与验证预算机制。
